matched_decode.workload: 10 requests; 128 input tokens and 256 output tokens per request
matched_decode.metric: reciprocal mean TPOT, tokens per second

points.name: BF16 + MTP2
points.description: The first vLLM baseline used the BF16 backbone and a two-token MTP draft.

points.name: INT4 group-128
points.description: The INT4 group-128 backbone reduced the active weight traffic. It kept sensitive layers at their source precision.

points.name: More GPU experts
points.description: More routed experts stayed on the GPUs. This reduced host-memory reads during decode.

points.name: Pinned H2D and host cache
points.description: Pinned transfers and a chunked host cache reduced the cost of an expert miss.

points.name: Static hot-96 cache
points.description: A fixed set kept 96 common experts on the GPUs. CUDA graphs could capture this stable path.

points.name: Mixed VMM hot-128
points.description: A mixed virtual-memory path kept 128 hot experts resident. All other experts stayed available in system memory.

points.name: Fused QSA
points.description: The fused QSA path reduced sparse-attention launch and selection overhead.

points.name: Humming and Marlin
points.description: Humming ran the target MoE path. Marlin ran the quantized MTP draft.

points.name: Dynamic LRU-100
points.description: A runtime LRU replaced the fixed expert list. It adapted the GPU cache to the current token stream.

points.name: Dynamic LRU-104
points.description: Four more resident experts gave the final gain in the matched short-decode test.

long_decode.workload: 128 input tokens and 4096 output tokens; warmed single request
